title: 5.1 Nutrients
description: Types of nutrients, their sources and functions

questions.question: What is food?
options: Only substances that come from animals
Any substance that is eaten, drunk, or taken into the body to sustain life, provide energy, promote growth, and repair tissues
Only plant-based materials consumed for energy
questions.answer: Any substance that is eaten, drunk, or taken into the body to sustain life, provide energy, promote growth, and repair tissues

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason why food is important for living things?
options: Increasing the speed of nerve impulses
Growth of new cells and tissues
questions.answer: Increasing the speed of nerve impulses

questions.question: What is nutrition?
options: The process of eating only vegetables
The process of digesting proteins only
The study of minerals in the body
The process of taking in food and converting it into energy and other vital nutrients required for life
questions.answer: The process of taking in food and converting it into energy and other vital nutrients required for life

questions.question: Which mode of nutrition involves organisms making their own food?
questions.answer: Autotrophic nutrition

questions.question: Organisms that cannot make their own food and depend on other organisms are said to have which type of nutrition?
questions.answer: Heterotrophic nutrition

questions.question: What are nutrients?
options: Chemical substances found in food that the body uses for growth, energy, and staying healthy
Substances that give food colour and flavour
Waste products eliminated from the body
Only the vitamins found in fruits
questions.answer: Chemical substances found in food that the body uses for growth, energy, and staying healthy

questions.question: How many kilojoules of energy does one gram of carbohydrate provide on average?
questions.answer: 16 kJ

questions.question: Which element is NOT part of the composition of carbohydrates?
questions.answer: Nitrogen

questions.question: The best sources of carbohydrates include:
options: Potatoes, bread, maize, rice, and cereals
questions.answer: Potatoes, bread, maize, rice, and cereals

questions.question: Which nutrient is primarily responsible for growth and building new cells in the body?
questions.answer: Proteins

questions.question: What elements make up proteins?
questions.answer: Carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, and nitrogen

questions.question: Which of the following is a good source of proteins from plants?
options: Beans, chickpeas, soy beans, and nuts
questions.answer: Beans, chickpeas, soy beans, and nuts

questions.question: How many kilojoules of energy does one gram of protein provide?
questions.answer: 17 kJ

questions.question: What is the main difference between fats and oils based on their physical state at room temperature?
options: Both are liquid at room temperature
Both are solid at room temperature
Fats are solid and oils are liquid at room temperature
Fats are liquid and oils are solid at room temperature
questions.answer: Fats are solid and oils are liquid at room temperature

questions.question: Fats are mainly obtained from which type of source?
options: Animal sources such as meat, milk, cheese, butter, and egg yolk
questions.answer: Animal sources such as meat, milk, cheese, butter, and egg yolk

questions.question: How many kilojoules of energy does one gram of lipid provide?
questions.answer: 37 kJ

questions.question: Which vitamins are fat-soluble and require dietary fat for absorption?
options: Vitamins E, K, B, and C
Vitamins A, D, E, and K
Vitamins A, B, C, and D
questions.answer: Vitamins A, D, E, and K

questions.question: What is the primary function of calcium in the human body?
options: Building teeth and bones, muscle contraction, and nerve impulse transmission
questions.answer: Building teeth and bones, muscle contraction, and nerve impulse transmission

questions.question: Which mineral is essential for the synthesis of hemoglobin in red blood cells?
questions.answer: Iron

questions.question: Iodine is important because it helps which gland to function properly?
questions.answer: Thyroid gland

questions.question: What are the best sources of iodine?
questions.answer: Iodized salt and seafood

questions.question: What is the role of water in the human body?
options: It acts as a solvent and transport medium for substances throughout the body
questions.answer: It acts as a solvent and transport medium for substances throughout the body

questions.question: What is dietary fibre and why is it important?
options: A type of protein that builds muscles
The indigestible part of plants that helps prevent constipation and keeps the colon healthy
A vitamin that boosts the immune system
questions.answer: The indigestible part of plants that helps prevent constipation and keeps the colon healthy

questions.question: A balanced diet is defined as:
options: A diet that includes only one type of food group
A diet that contains all nutrients in the correct amount and proportion
A diet that contains only carbohydrates
A diet that excludes all fats
questions.answer: A diet that contains all nutrients in the correct amount and proportion

questions.question: Which group of people requires a higher protein diet for muscle development?
questions.answer: Athletes
